newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia has another national car in design stage.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia has another national car in design stage.

text.p: Indonesia's national car controversy took on an added dimension on Tuesday when Research and Technology Minister Jusuf Habibie said one of his departments would press ahead with its own car design.
Habibie told a parliamentary commission hearing in a written report that the Maleo vehicle project under the Strategic Industry Body (BPIS) had entered a second stage of development.
"Up until now we have already finished the first phase of the design development by BPIS in cooperation with Millard Design Australia, an automotive engineering design company," the report said.
"The activities in phase two (the detailed engineering design and testing) will be finished at the end of 1997," Habibie said.
"A large part of these activities will involve technical experts from Indonesia's strategic industries," he added.
The Maleo, reportedly a 1,600 cc passenger vehicle, is the brainchild of the German-trained aeronautical engineer Habibie and has been referred to as "Habibie's Volkswagen".
Local production has been set for 1998, with a target capacity of more than 100,000 units a year at a cost of 20 million rupiah ($8,628).
Reports in July said Habibie was considering using a motor developed by the Orbital Engine Corporation

In February, Indonesia gave special tax and tariff breaks to PT Putra Timor Nasional to make a national car in partnership with Kia Motors of South Korea. The company is controlled by President Suharto's youngest son, Hutomo Mandala Putra.
The controversial move was attacked by Japan, Europe and the United States for violating World Trade Organisation rules.

The 1,600 cc Timor sedan enters the market next month at a price of 35 million rupiah ($15,100), considerably cheaper than existing models, with the company initially selling fully built-up vehicles before beginning local assembly next March.
In July, Bimantara Citra, a firm controlled by another of Suharto's sons, Bambang Trihatmodjo, unveiled two new cars in conjunction with Hyundai Motors of South Korea.
The 1,500cc and 1,600cc Bimantara Citra and Bimantara Nenggala sedans would sell at 39.9 million rupiah ($17,213) and 59.5 million rupiah ($25,668).
